title: Trump Backs a United Ireland in Dublin as Houthis Push Toward Bab al-Mandab and Saudi Arabia Shuts Its East-West Oil Pipeline
subhead: On a two-day visit to Dublin, Donald Trump said Irish unification would happen 'eventually,' a remark that reverberated across the Atlantic even as Irish officials insist no policy change is coming. Meanwhile, the Iran war compounds: the Houthis have seized large stretches of Yemen's Red Sea coast toward Bab al-Mandab, and Saudi Arabia has shut the East-West pipeline that carries roughly 4-5% of global oil supply after a drone strike launched from Iraq.

sections.heading: Trump Raises Irish Unity on Dublin Trip
sections.body:
During a two-day visit to Ireland, US President Donald Trump said Irish unification would 'eventually' happen, first in a free-wheeling press conference and then again, almost as an opening remark, in a speech to Irish and Irish-American business leaders at the US ambassador's residence. The BBC reports the comments quickly became the day's main transatlantic headline, coming days after Trump again criticised the UK's support for his military operation in Iran.

Both US officials and Irish politicians moved to contain the fallout. Former Republican congressman Mick Mulvaney, Trump's first-term special envoy to Northern Ireland, told the BBC the remarks 'do not represent a shift in US foreign policy' and emphasised continued US commitment to the Good Friday Agreement. Democratic congressman Brendan Boyle cited 'bipartisan support' for the deal. BBC analysis notes Trump's audience may have been as much the US Irish-American voting bloc ahead of November's midterms as the government in Dublin.
sections.whyItMatters: The remarks inject uncertainty into US-UK-Ireland relations at a delicate moment, when Washington is already pressing London over the Iran campaign and the UK's posture on Northern Ireland remains sensitive. Even if it is not policy, the signal tests alliance cohesion in the Atlantic.

sections.heading: Houthis Roll Up Yemen's Red Sea Coast Toward Bab al-Mandab
sections.body:
The Iranian-backed Houthis have captured as much as 130km (81 miles) of Yemen's strategically important coastline along the Tihamah coastal plain, according to estimates cited by the BBC, after a lightning advance that has taken most observers by surprise and overrun significant National Resistance territory in a matter of days. It is the group's most impressive military move in years, coming on top of Thursday's seizure of the Red Sea port of Mokha, about 80km north of Bab al-Mandab.

If the Houthis also control key islands in the Red Sea, including Perim in the narrowest part of the Bab al-Mandab, their ability to disrupt international shipping is greatly enhanced. Chatham House fellow Farea al-Muslimi told the BBC this means Iran, directly and through proxies, now holds sway over two of the world's most important maritime chokepoints - Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab - which he said could cover more than 35% of global fuel and oil trade. The UN says at least 76,000 people have been displaced in Yemen since July, a figure that has quadrupled in the past week, warning of a 'rapidly worsening displacement crisis unfolding by the hour.'
sections.whyItMatters: Territorial control of Bab al-Mandab is a more durable lever over global shipping than hit-and-run attacks, and it hands Tehran influence over two chokepoints simultaneously. The US, wary of opening a new front in an already unpopular war, is expanding support for Saudi Arabia without committing to direct strikes, per Axios reporting cited by the BBC.

sections.heading: Saudi Arabia Shuts East-West Pipeline After Iraqi-Launched Drone Strike
sections.body:
Riyadh has shut its East-West pipeline after a drone attack launched from Iraq's Maysan province, which borders Iran, struck the line. The 1,200km pipeline has been carrying an estimated 4-5% of global oil supply as an alternative route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, according to Reuters, citing ship tracking and analysts. Saudi Arabia's foreign ministry confirmed some injuries and damage and said the kingdom reserves the right to take all necessary measures to protect its facilities, while choosing not to retaliate immediately following a call from Iraq's prime minister.

Iraq said it has removed the operations commander in Maysan and opened an investigation. The Gulf Cooperation Council condemned the attack as a 'dangerous escalation.' Yemeni government-aligned forces have since struck back against Houthi positions around Mokha, destroying vehicles and killing fighters, according to spokesman Majid al-Nuzaili. Saudi Arabia has previously struck Iran-backed militias in Iraq alongside the US over similar drone attacks on its facilities.
sections.whyItMatters: With Hormuz already closed since earlier this year, knocking the East-West pipeline offline tightens the squeeze on Saudi exports and global oil markets at the exact moment the Houthis threaten the Red Sea route. The Iraqi origin of the strike shows Iran's ability to hit Saudi energy infrastructure from a third country's soil, complicating any US-Saudi response.

sections.heading: Ukraine Braces for 'Toughest Winter' Since 2022 Invasion
sections.body:
A senior UN official has warned Ukraine faces its toughest winter since Russia's 2022 full-scale invasion, telling the BBC there is a 'race against the clock' to repair the power network before temperatures that can reach -20C. Alexander De Croo, head of the UN development agency, said Russia's 'very systematic' targeting of civilian energy infrastructure, transmission lines, shops and shopping malls could push the country toward a humanitarian catastrophe if power, water and sewage systems collapse.

The warning comes as Russia intensifies around-the-clock aerial attacks on Kyiv and other cities, increasingly using faster jet-powered drones that are harder to intercept. Five people were killed and 67 wounded in a daytime Russian drone strike on a shopping mall in Pavlohrad on Thursday, Ukrainian officials say, following mall attacks in Zaporizhzhia and Sumy. Ukraine continues to strike deep into Russian territory - Russia reported a Ukrainian seaborne drone attack on Sochi in which 28 people were wounded - and two people were killed when Russian drones hit a border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova.
sections.whyItMatters: The energy war is becoming the decisive front of the Russia-Ukraine conflict this winter. Russia's apparent shift to harder-to-intercept jet drones is designed to break Ukrainian civilian resilience, and the humanitarian stakes could reshape international pressure on both Moscow and Western allies to push for a negotiated outcome.

sections.heading: European Infrastructure-Sabotage Pattern Widens
sections.body:
Authorities in northern France are investigating whether Friday evening's derailment of a passenger train between Rouen and Caen, in which 44 people were injured and an 18-year-old woman was airlifted in critical condition, was a malicious act. Prosecutor Sébastien Gallois said the leading theory is that a piece of rail was present on the track, and the reason for its presence is unknown. The train's black box has been seized and a court-appointed expert called in, with 186 passengers on board.

The incident follows this week's report that Bulgaria is investigating a fire at a weapons site that the owner calls sabotage, with officials not ruling out 'outside interference.' It is the latest in a stretch of European infrastructure incidents, adding to earlier attacks and disruptions that have put critical transport and industrial facilities on alert across the continent.
sections.whyItMatters: Whether or not Russia is ultimately implicated, the clustering of suspected sabotage at European transport and defence-industry sites is intensifying scrutiny of hybrid-war threats and pressing NATO members to harden critical infrastructure ahead of winter pressure points.

bottomLine: Two reinforcing pressures define the day. In the Middle East, the Iran war is compounding: the Houthis have surged onto Yemen's Red Sea coast toward Bab al-Mandab, giving Tehran leverage over a second global chokepoint to match Hormuz, while a drone strike launched from Iraq forced Saudi Arabia to shut the East-West pipeline carrying 4-5% of global oil supply. Separately, Trump's remarks in favour of Irish unity unsettled transatlantic ties even as officials insisted US policy had not changed, and the UN warned Ukraine faces its toughest winter yet as Russia turns to harder-to-intercept drones against its energy grid. The through-line is an international system under strain on energy, alliance and infrastructure fronts, with no sign of an off-ramp in the Iran crisis or the war in Ukraine.
